description: We are a team from Annie Wright Schools! This is our first year at NASA Space Apps, and we could not be more excited!
summary: We developed a mars rover game that tasks the player to locate and repair inactive rovers scattered around the martian terrain. It addresses the challenges by providing a game more accessible to younger children that shows them how to work with what they have, just like engineers often do. This matters because it teaches them not only about Mars rovers, but about exploration and resource management.
details: Rover Route lets players control a rover that can repair both inactive rovers and itself after taking damage from craters across the Martian landscape. The rover features a built-in battery system that depletes over time as the game progresses, resulting in a game over if it runs empty. The map consists of nine sections with varying crater positions. Every time the player enters a section, the crater layout shifts to keep the gameplay randomized, and the locations of the inactive rovers are also randomized at the start of every game. Periodically, dust storms—inspired by real Martian weather—appear and reduce visibility of the terrain, the rover's location, and the battery, health, and repair bars. We coded the game using microStudio. Through Rover Route, we aimed to simulate the Martian environment and showcase the challenges rovers face to complete their missions. To play, use the W, A, S, and D keys to move, make contact with another rover and press E to repair it, and press Q to heal your own rover.
